Numerical inverse kinematics

Source: R/inverse-kinematics.R
robot_ik.Rd

Solves \(FK(q) \approx T^*\) for a target pose (or position) of frame. The error is \(e = (p^* - p, \log(R^* R^\top))\) in world coordinates, a proper SO(3) orientation error rather than a difference of Euler angles. With \(W = \mathrm{diag}(weights)\) the solver minimizes \(e^\top W e = \|W^{1/2} e\|^2\); residual is its square root. Joints that sit on a limit and would be pushed outward are frozen for that step (an active set), so the other joints keep moving. Methods:

Usage

robot_ik(
  robot,
  target,
  initial = NULL,
  frame = NULL,
  method = c("levenberg_marquardt", "damped_least_squares", "pseudoinverse"),
  weights = NULL,
  tol = 1e-10,
  max_iterations = 200,
  lambda = 0.01,
  max_step = 0.5,
  restarts = 5,
  respect_limits = TRUE,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

target

A robot_pose (SE(3)) or a length-3 position. A position target sets the orientation weights to zero.

initial

Initial configuration (defaults to robot_home()).

frame

Frame to place (NULL for the end effector).

method

"levenberg_marquardt", "damped_least_squares", or "pseudoinverse".

weights

Length-6 nonnegative weights for \((x, y, z, \omega_x, \omega_y, \omega_z)\) errors. Use zeros for unconstrained directions, for example c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1) for a planar arm with a pose target.

tol

Convergence tolerance on the weighted error norm.

max_iterations

Maximum iterations per attempt.

lambda

Initial damping.

max_step

Largest change of any joint variable in one iteration (radians or meters). Steps are scaled down to this size, which keeps iterations started near singular configurations from jumping far.

restarts

Maximum number of extra attempts from random initial configurations, used only while the solver has not converged.

respect_limits

Project iterates onto the joint limits.

seed

Seed for the restart configurations (default 1, so results are reproducible); the global random state is never changed.

Value

A robot_ik_solution list with q, converged, residual, position_error, orientation_error (radians), iterations, attempts, active_limits (names of joints at a limit), singular (rank-deficient weighted Jacobian at the solution), reach_bound (an upper bound on the reachable distance from the base) and target_distance.

Details

  • "levenberg_marquardt" (default): \(\Delta q = (J^\top W J + \lambda \mu I)^{-1} J^\top W e\), where \(\mu\) is the largest diagonal entry of \(J^\top W J\), with \(\lambda\) decreased after successful steps and increased after rejected steps.

  • "damped_least_squares": \(\Delta q = J^\top (J J^\top + \lambda^2 I)^{-1} e\) with fixed \(\lambda\), plus backtracking.

  • "pseudoinverse": \(\Delta q = J^{+} e\) from a truncated SVD, plus backtracking.

With respect_limits = TRUE each iterate is projected onto the joint limits. When the solve from initial fails, up to restarts further attempts start from random configurations within the limits; the best result is returned. Numerical IK can fail even for reachable targets and never proves that a target is unreachable.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar2")
sol <- robot_ik(robot, c(1, 1, 0), initial = c(0.3, 0.3))
sol$q
#>        joint1        joint2 
#> -2.669000e-13  1.570796e+00 
sol$converged
#> [1] TRUE
